answer.why: As an insider, 'Confirmed & Substantive' made me laugh straight away because it's the exact phrasing of appointment status in the service, and it signals the designer knows the real texture of the job. 'Minister Salary' is the obvious hook, but it feels like clickbait that invites a rant about benchmarks, and I've read that comment thread a hundred times. I'd tap the quieter one out of curiosity, though I suspect most people in a store wouldn't.
answer.expect_minister_salary: A satirical or political-grievance game, probably about chasing the big pay package. I'd expect it to be shallow on the details, with cartoonish scholars and a lot of jokes about the million-dollar benchmark, and I'd brace for the wrong grades and titles. It would get clicks from outsiders and sighs from colleagues.
answer.expect_confirmed_substantive: A dry, insider-flavoured career sim about the grind of the service: probation, appraisals, getting confirmed in your post, acting appointments versus substantive ones. I'd expect it to be quieter and more accurate, with in-jokes only public servants get, and a slower, more bureaucratic humour. Outsiders might find the name baffling and not know what it means.

best_moment.what: Made Perm Sec MHA with 'outstanding, clear potential for wider responsibility'. The appraisal wording was exactly how it reads in real life, and it felt earned by years of quiet, honest work.

worst_moment.what: The GRC election loss. I made the choice knowing REP was 54 against the 60 needed, and the result was a flat card with no campaign texture, so it felt like a number being revealed rather than a story I played.

skip_year.why: The missed school concert for a deadline was set up as a cost at home, but nothing at home ever came back. It was a setup with no payoff, so I'd skip it.

callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Ending card says it removed my ceiling inside the service altogether

callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Legacy line: people I trained quote me in rooms I will never enter, two say I'm why they stayed

callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Exposure line: file is clean enough to be boring

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Y21 missed the school concert for a deadline

answer.held_back_by: My own candour. Telling people exactly why things would fail kept my integrity at 100 but cost me standing and reputation, and politics needed a REP I never built. Being right in the room is not the same as being liked outside it.
answer.ending_fair_why: Yes. 48.2% in a GRC I entered knowing the REP gap is a believable near-miss, and the card owned that it was never about me. Retiring as Perm Sec with a clean file is a good outcome, not a failure.
answer.chase_next: The single-seat or minister route, by building REP above 60 first, probably by taking the Pingat and public-facing postings, to see whether candour can survive being popular.
answer.play_again_why: I want to see the politics branch, but the run was long and the ending was somewhat predictable. I'd wait a few days first.

tone_breaks.line: When you joined, your file estimated your potential at Permanent Secretary... You were not told.
tone_breaks.note: Potential ratings do exist, but a 'ceiling' that the game reveals and then 'removes' at 27 is a bit too neat. The real CEP is never that explicit, so I'd soften it.

tone_breaks.line: You shook every hand in that ward
tone_breaks.note: A GRC team contests a division or ward as a group, so 'the ward' for one person reads slightly off. Also, 'Lost the Ward' is a bit casual for a GRC loss.

answer.title_fit_why: The game is about slow, honest accumulation and what that does to a career, not about the pay. The salary mostly sat in the background, and the title I'd remember is the one about being confirmed in a post.
